author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces — the page and the machine-readable list — can be narrowed to a single specialty named in the address. Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case; a blank name narrows nothing; a specialty no veterinarian holds gives an empty listing; paging keeps the narrowing.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is asked for that specialty, then only those veterinarians are listed, still a page at a time.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable form is asked for that specialty, then it carries only those veterinarians.
Given a specialty named in different letter case, when either form is asked for it, then the same veterinarians are listed.
Given only the first letters of a specialty name, when either form is asked for it, then no veterinarian is listed.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is asked for it, then the listing is returned empty rather than reported as a failure.
Given a specialty name that is empty or all spaces, when either form is asked for it, then every veterinarian is listed.
Given no specialty named at all, when either form is opened, then it lists every veterinarian as it did before narrowing existed.
Given a narrowed listing longer than one page, when the reader moves to the next page, then the narrowing still holds.
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed under each of them.
Edge case 3: a veterinarian holding no specialty appears only when no specialty is named.
Edge case 4: a specialty name carrying leading or trailing spaces matches nothing, because matching is on the whole name.
Edge case 5: the number of pages of a narrowed listing counts the narrowed veterinarians, not the whole directory.
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty — the narrowing is a URL contract only in this slice
free-text veterinarian search, which stays declined under NG-9
narrowing the directory by anything other than specialty
narrowing any listing other than the veterinarian directory
notes: Non-goal ADR: docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-vet-directory-filtering.md records the NG-9 narrowing. docs/adr/README.md's index still needs the row for it — that file is outside the product expert's write scope. One fresh requirement was minted for the reinstated machine-readable surface and its first capability, per the owner's decision; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and unreused, and the Superseded entry and the Veterinarian directory known-defect note were updated accordingly. Two narrowest readings were taken where the intake left a choice, and both are recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md rather than raised as a consultation: a specialty name with surrounding spaces matches nothing (only an empty or all-spaces name counts as absent), and no page control is added on either surface.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the existing vet feature package and adds no type. Narrowing is two new Spring Data derived reads on VetRepository (paged for the page, unpaged Collection for the machine-readable form), a second request parameter on each VetController handler, and specialty-carrying pagination links in vets/vetList.html. What makes this new ground rather than covered is the cache: VetRepository's existing reads are @Cacheable("vets"), and CacheConfiguration creates that cache with statistics only, so Caffeine backs it with no size limit and no eviction. Annotating the narrowed reads the same way would put caller-supplied free text into the key of an unevicted cache. Decision recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-lookups.md: the narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable. docs/system-design.md now states the cache's scope under Contracts, carries the requirement id on the five vet rows, and gains a Threat Model row for caller-chosen cache keys. The machine-readable route left Known Defects, since it is a supported surface again.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a paged narrowed read and an unpaged narrowed read; neither is annotated @Cacheable, unlike the two findAll siblings
VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty request parameter and picks between the narrowed and unnarrowed paged read; the model carries the active specialty so the view can rebuild links
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same parameter and picks between the narrowed and unnarrowed collection read; the Vets wrapper and its serialization are unchanged
vets/vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty forward on every page, first, previous, next, and last link
No schema, seed-data, message-bundle, or dependency change: specialty names are already seeded and the page renders no new text

patterns.description: Repository pattern, in force: an optional narrowing expressed as a Spring Data derived query taking a Pageable. findByLastNameStartingWith is the shape the two new vet reads follow, with a property path across the specialties association instead of a scalar.

Web controller pattern, in force: an absent or empty search term is normalized at the binding boundary and then delegated, rather than branching on a domain rule. The vet controller's blank-means-unnarrowed branch is the same shape.

Web controller row: holds no business rule. The blank-means-absent branch is request normalization plus delegate selection, not a new rule; the whole-name case-insensitive matching rule lives in the derived query, not in the controller. Reviewers should read it against this line rather than as a fresh violation of the recorded controller-rules deviation.

risks.risk: Spring Data must resolve the property path across the specialties association. The camel-case form findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase can bind to an unintended path if Vet ever gains a specialtiesName-shaped property.
risks.mitigation: Declare the underscore-disambiguated form findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase, which pins the traversal explicitly.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is a FetchType.EAGER @ManyToMany. A paged query that both joins the collection for the predicate and fetch-joins it can mispage or mis-count, which would break the acceptance criterion that a narrowed listing's page count reflects the narrowed veterinarians (edge case 5). Hibernate may also fall back to in-memory pagination for a collection fetch join.
risks.mitigation: Assert total pages and total items on a narrowed listing directly, not just the rows on the first page. If Hibernate paginates in memory or the count double-counts, replace the derived read with an explicit paged JPQL query plus a matching countQuery.

risks.risk: vetList.html builds pagination links by string concatenation inside @{'...'} with __${}__ preprocessing. Appending a caller-supplied specialty that way leaves it unencoded, so a name containing an ampersand or a hash corrupts the link, and the value is echoed into the page unescaped.
risks.mitigation: Switch the links to Thymeleaf's URL parameter syntax, @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes each value and omits a null parameter. Do not concatenate the specialty into the URL string.

risks.risk: The blank rule and the surrounding-spaces rule pull in opposite directions and are easy to conflate. An empty or all-spaces value narrows nothing, but a non-blank value carrying leading or trailing spaces must match nothing. OwnerController strips its search term, so copying that precedent verbatim would break the edge case.
risks.mitigation: Test for blankness only, and pass the value through unstripped. Cover both directions: the all-spaces value listing every veterinarian, and the padded valid name listing none.

risks.risk: A caller can mint cache entries by naming values the application does not choose. The vets cache has no size limit and no eviction.
risks.mitigation: Leave the narrowed reads unannotated, per docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-lookups.md. The threat-model row records that the pre-existing page-keyed exposure is unchanged and that bounding the cache stays an open question.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Design writes this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-lookups.md (new), docs/adr/README.md index rows for both 2026-08-21 ADRs (the non-goal row the prd-entry flagged, plus the new one), and docs/system-design.md (Contracts rows and cache-scope statement, Threat Model row, Known Defects row removed, provenance defect count corrected from four to three, Settled-since-the-survey note). Coverage claims rest on grep and direct file reads; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so the weaker basis applies. One defect to hand on, in a file outside my ownership: docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-vet-directory-filtering.md links ../prd.md#req-vetsspecialtyfilter-001, but docs/prd.md carries no such heading, so the anchor is dead. The nearest live target is ../prd.md#veterinarian-directory. The file is the product expert's, so it is flagged rather than edited. Open Question 5 (vet cache invalidation) stays open and is now cross-referenced from the new ADR.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this round, and this is a gap in the check rather than a clean result: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependencyCheck plugin (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11), and this reviewer has no network access. The risk this round is nil because the change set touches no build file and adds no dependency, so the resolved artifact set is unchanged from the last verified state. Closing the gap generally needs CI or a human to run an NVD match against the CycloneDX SBOM the build already produces; it pairs with Open Question 6 (no dependency lockfile) in docs/system-design.md.

Not a defect, just the boundary worth remembering: the specialty value is length-unbounded apart from the servlet container's query-string cap, and each narrowed request now costs an uncached database round trip where the unnarrowed page is served from cache. That is the correct trade against cache poisoning, and rate limiting is already a recorded non-control for this demonstration; no action in this slice.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the narrowing is a Spring Data derived query (VetRepository.findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase, paged and unpaged). No query text is concatenated anywhere in the change; the caller-supplied name reaches JPA as a bound parameter. Meets security-principles.md 'Injection into data access'.

Cross-site scripting: vetList.html rewrites all five pagination links from the old @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} string-concatenation-plus-preprocessing form to Thymeleaf parameter syntax @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. The value is URL-encoded by the link builder and attribute-escaped by the engine, so an ampersand, hash, quote, or javascript:/markup payload in ?specialty= cannot break out of the href. Class sweep: grep for '__${' and 'th:utext' across src/main/resources/templates/ now returns no hits at all, so this change removes the last template-expression-preprocessing sites rather than adding one. Default output escaping stays on; the specialty is not rendered as page text anywhere.

Cache-key poisoning: the two narrowed reads deliberately carry no @Cacheable, unlike their findAll siblings, so caller-chosen text never becomes a key in the unbounded, evictionless 'vets' Caffeine cache. The divergence from the neighbouring cached reads is justified inline in the VetRepository javadoc and in docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-lookups.md, satisfying the Pattern Consistency clause. docs/system-design.md gains a matching Threat Model row that correctly scopes the residual page-keyed exposure as pre-existing and unchanged.

Widening the exposed surface: no new route. Both handlers gain one optional scalar @RequestParam on already-public directory data; no mass-assignment surface (no command object, no binder change), no management-endpoint change, no new dependency (build.gradle is not in the change set).

Input handling at the boundary: narrowingSpecialty() normalizes absent/empty/blank to null at the controller edge and delegates, with no defensive re-checking downstream. No filesystem or classpath resource is composed from the value, no shell or process execution, no deserialization entry point, no logging of the value (so no log-injection vector), and no regex, so no ReDoS surface. Greps for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec(/enableDefaultTyping/JsonTypeInfo//tmp/ across src/main/java return only pre-existing, unrelated hits.

No secret introduced: a case-insensitive sweep of the whole change set for password/secret/token/apikey/credential/private_key matches one pre-existing docs/system-design.md Threat Model line and nothing else.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All seven new specialty-narrowing tests use the pre-2026-07-31 `should{Outcome}` naming (shouldFindVetsHoldingTheNamedSpecialty, shouldFindEveryVetHoldingTheNamedSpecialtyWithoutPaging, shouldListAVetHoldingSeveralSpecialtiesUnderEachOfThem, shouldMatchTheSpecialtyNameIgnoringCase, shouldMatchOnTheWholeSpecialtyNameOnly, shouldFindNoVetForASpecialtyNobodyHolds, shouldCountTheNarrowedVetsRatherThanTheWholeDirectoryWhenPaging) rather than the mandated BDD school `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` (testing-principles.md § Test Naming: 'Applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward... a slice that touches a test renames only that test'). The sibling file VetControllerTests.java gets this right in the same slice (theVetListShouldShowOnlyVetsHoldingTheNamedSpecialty etc.), so the inconsistency is within this change alone, not inherited debt. Matching the host file's older convention is not the applicable rule here — the naming school is a written-date rule, not a file rule.
findings.fix: Rename the seven new ClinicServiceTests methods to the BDD form, e.g. shouldFindVetsHoldingTheNamedSpecialty -> theRepositoryShouldFindVetsHoldingTheNamedSpecialty, shouldMatchOnTheWholeSpecialtyNameOnly -> theRepositoryShouldMatchOnlyOnTheWholeSpecialtyName, and so on for the remaining five.

findings.description: Both tests pack two independent scenarios (empty string vs. all-spaces; first-letters-only vs. padded-with-spaces) into one straight-line test body via two separate act+assert pairs, instead of a @ParameterizedTest — the checklist's named default AUTOFIX ('Missing @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases') and testing-principles.md's edge-case guidance ('@ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource covers all edge cases').
findings.fix: Convert each to a @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource carrying the two data points (e.g. specialty value + expected-empty/expected-full flag), one assertion per invocation.

findings.description: The JSON-surface blank test only exercises the all-spaces case ("   "); it never exercises the empty-string case. The HTML-surface counterpart (theVetListShouldListEveryVetWhenTheSpecialtyIsBlank) exercises both. The PRD acceptance criterion ('a specialty name that is empty or all spaces... every veterinarian is listed') is therefore only half-covered on the machine-readable surface.
findings.fix: Add the empty-string case to theVetJsonShouldListEveryVetWhenTheSpecialtyIsBlank (or fold it into the @ParameterizedTest conversion above alongside the all-spaces case).

approved_aspects: Repository-level tests exercise the real H2-backed query (ClinicServiceTests), matching the brief's real-I/O-for-integration rule; VetControllerTests' MockitoBean stub of VetRepository is the pre-existing, sanctioned controller-boundary pattern already used in this file

The Hibernate collection-fetch-join mis-paging risk the design-block flagged is directly covered: shouldCountTheNarrowedVetsRatherThanTheWholeDirectoryWhenPaging asserts totalElements, totalPages, and content size against the real database

The unencoded-URL-punctuation risk the design-block flagged is directly covered: theVetListShouldEncodeASpecialtyCarryingUrlPunctuationIntoItsLinks asserts percent-encoding and absence of the raw ampersand
The blank-vs-padded-spaces distinction the design-block called out as easy to conflate is covered in both directions (all-spaces narrows nothing; padded valid name matches nothing)
Case-insensitive and whole-name-only matching are both covered at the repository layer where the matching logic actually lives
Test data uses named locals (heldByNoVet, firstLettersOnly, paddedWithSpaces, withAnAmpersand) rather than mystery literals, and reuses the existing james()/helen() factories
All new and existing VetControllerTests/ClinicServiceTests pass (13 and 19 tests respectively, 0 failures)

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Ten files, one module, no sensitive paths: two Java files in the vet package, one template, and five docs. The widest reach is vetList.html, whose five pagination links were all rewritten and so also serve the unnarrowed page every existing reader sees; that path is pinned by a test asserting the plain page-two link carries no specialty parameter.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk against the requirement and found nothing the diff's shape would not predict. Narrowing is a Spring Data derived query with a bound parameter, blank-vs-padded normalization sits in one helper used identically by both handlers, the two narrowed reads deliberately omit the cache annotation so caller text never keys the unevicted vets cache, and the template rewrite replaces string-preprocessed URLs with parameter syntax that URL-encodes rather than concatenates.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes against the real H2 seed data (radiology is held by Leary and Stevens, Douglas holds surgery and dentistry) rather than restating the implementation, and each would fail against a plausible wrong implementation: prefix matching, trimming the padded name, a page count taken from the whole directory, an unencoded ampersand in a link, or a dropped specialty when paging onward. Both the page and the machine-readable surface are covered, including the empty and all-spaces cases the second review round closed.

reviewer_hedging.note: The final round approved with no recommendations, and the three round-one test findings were all fixable autofixes that were made and re-verified. Two parked notes remain and neither is a reservation about this change: code quality flags the five-fold ternary duplication in vetList.html as pre-existing shape it extends rather than introduces, and security reports it could not run an NVD supply-chain match, a standing tooling and network gap whose applicability here is nil because the change set touches no build file or dependency.

scope_deviation.note: The change matches the intake decision term for term, including the three product calls the owner made there: NG-9 narrowed rather than dropped, a fresh requirement id with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn and unreused, and a URL contract with no page control added. The single design revision was bookkeeping (declaring two doc paths the audit caught as uncovered), not an architectural change, and the row's zero build retries is consistent with counting only failures after that revision.

rationale: Read every hunk; the code does exactly what the requirement describes, with the boundary cases pinned against real seed data. Confirm one thing that outlives the code: this slice redraws PRD non-goal NG-9 and lifts the machine-readable vet route out of Known Defects. Both are quoted owner decisions, so check the recorded wording is the boundary you meant.
